summary: Georg Wilhelm Freytag worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1807–1811) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1815–1819), later holding posts at Göttingen (1811–1813), Königsberg (~1812–1814), and the University of Bonn (1819–1861).

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Freytag specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as an instructor at Göttingen (1811–1813) and professor at the University of Bonn (1819–1861).

Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, the University of Tübingen and Tübinger Stift (~1788–1793), and the University of Jena under F. W. J. Schelling. He held academic posts at Jena (~1801–1807), Heidelberg (~1816–1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1953–1956) and completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1956–1965), later working at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Jena, TU Dresden, and Leipzig University. He held professorships at Leipzig University (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889), and was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1889).

George A. Kennedy specialized in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1935) under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke, and held an academic post at Yale University (~1935–1960).

George A. Keyworth works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and completed his PhD at UCLA (2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Ronald Egan, William F. Powell, and Shuizhao Wang. He held posts at CU Boulder and the University of Saskatchewan.

Linguist and Indologist George Abraham Grierson was educated at St Bees School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1873–1903), directed the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and was a governor of SOAS (1917–1925).
George C. O. Haas was an Indologist. He served as the recording secretary of the American Oriental Society (~1913–1918) and worked as an editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

George Cardona worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at NYU, Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill and Paul Thieme, and with several traditional pandits. He was a fellow at CASBS (1971–1972) and held a professorship at the University of Pennsylvania (~1960–2011).

George Chemparathy specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Paul Hacker and Erich Frauwallner (~1964–1969), and he held academic posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

George Cowgill worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2018).
George Croom Robertson was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London, where he subsequently held an academic post (~1866–1892).

George Cœdès worked in Indology, Sinology, and archaeology. He studied at EPHE and Berlin under Finot, Lévi, Foucher, and Pischel. He served as director of EFEO (1929–1947), headed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and held posts in Paris.

George D. Bond works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD from Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he served as Professor of Religion (~1974–2012).

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard University (1903–1905). He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George Derwent Thomson worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at King's College, Cambridge (~1922–1925) and Trinity College Dublin (~1925–1927), and held posts at the University of Cambridge (~1927–1931) and the University of Birmingham (~1936–1970).

George Devereux studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, INALCO under Marcel Mauss, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1963–1985) and Paris Descartes University (~1972–1985).

George Eugene Dunkel is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania in 1976 and held academic posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1978), Princeton University (1978–1986), and the University of Zurich (from 1986).

George Foot Moore was a scholar of religious studies. He studied at Yale (1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877), and held professorships at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Harvard University (1902–1928), along with a guest professorship in Berlin (1909–1910).
